Researched 2026-11-17 as an add-on to the forex roadmap. Education, not investment advice.

Verification tags are the same as in resources.js: ok = page opened or search returned matching details, part = only third-party summaries back the details, unv = from memory, check before relying on it.

1. Short answer

  • SMC / ICT is not in the roadmap. The only mention is one line in Phase 3 of index.html: most "smart money" vocabulary renames ideas in Wyckoff and Grimes. None of the 202 resources is about SMC, Wyckoff, volume profile, footprint charts or auction market theory.
  • "Order flow" is in the roadmap, but only in one of its two meanings (see section 2).
  • You have already done more SMC work in code than in study. projects/Trading-EA/ has about ten SMC robots (wiki: projects/Trading-EA/wiki/index.md). None has a proven edge yet.
  • The evidence is mixed in a specific way. One idea behind SMC (stops cluster just beyond obvious levels) is backed by peer-reviewed FX research. But that research found price keeps going when it reaches the stops; it did not find the sweep-then-reverse move that SMC trades. The trading rules built on top (order blocks, FVGs, sweeps as entries) mostly do not beat random entries in the open tests that exist.

What it isA story read from candles: which side is in control, where stops sit, which zone price should return toMeasured buying and selling: delta, footprint, order book (DOM), volume profile
Data neededPlain OHLC candlesEvery trade with bid/ask, on an exchange
Works on spot FX?Yes (it is only candles)No. Spot FX has no central exchange; MT5 "volume" is tick count. Use CME FX futures (6E, 6B, 6J; gold = GC)
In the roadmap nowMissingPartly: academic FX papers (Evans & Lyons, Lyons) in Phases 2 and 7, plus ../concepts/order_flow.md and ../concepts/vwap_volume_profile_explained.md
Theory behind itWyckoff, price action, stop-huntingAuction market theory, market microstructure

4. What the evidence says

Part of the mechanism is real (peer-reviewed):

  • Osler (2003), Journal of Finance, "Currency Orders and Exchange Rate Dynamics". Data: about 9,700 real stop-loss and take-profit orders at a large bank. Take-profit orders cluster at round numbers; stop-loss orders cluster just beyond them. Take-profits tend to reverse a move at the level; stops tend to extend it once the level breaks. ok https://www.newyorkfed.org/medialibrary/media/research/staff_reports/sr125.pdf
  • Osler (2005), J. of International Money and Finance, "Stop-loss orders and price cascades in currency markets". Trends speed up when price reaches stop clusters. The effect lasts hours, not days, and she does not claim stops are the main cause of big moves. ok https://www.newyorkfed.org/medialibrary/media/research/staff_reports/sr150.pdf
  • Kavajecz & Odders-White (2004), Review of Financial Studies, "Technical Analysis and Liquidity Provision". Support and resistance levels line up with peaks of resting orders in the book. Stock-market data, not FX; later studies repeated it on Taiwanese and Chinese stocks. ok https://ideas.repec.org/a/oup/rfinst/v17y2004i4p1043-1071.html

So "liquidity rests beyond obvious levels" is a fair description of the market. Note what these papers do not say:

  • that price reverses after taking the stops. Osler's documented effect is continuation through the level for some hours. The SMC sweep-and-reverse trade is the opposite bet at the same level, so test both;
  • that a bank hunts your stop on purpose, or that an order block marks where an institution will buy again.

The trading rules mostly fail open tests:

  • StatOasis (Ali Casey, Sep 2026): order block, FVG, sweep and OTE as fixed rules on daily SPY/QQQ/DIA/IWM, against a coin-flip entry and buy-and-hold. Of 32 t-statistics only one reached 2. Order blocks beat random entries in most variants but never with significance; FVG edge was about zero; nothing beat buy-and-hold. Limits: daily stock ETFs, long-only, no costs. ok https://statoasis.com/overfit/research/ict-backtest-what-survives
  • Northmark / fxbroker-compass (Aug 2026): six SMC-style rules, 328 settings, 995,550 trades on FX, gold and US30. None passed; average −2.13 pips a trade; win rates 26–36%; entries were within −3 to +7 points of random. On 15-minute bars costs were 30–60% of the stop. Weak source: broker-affiliate site, written with AI help, period and exact rules not published. ok (opened) https://www.fxbroker-compass.com/en/blog/fx-order-block-fvg-liquidity-sweep-verification
  • Vendor posts claiming 60–80% win rates give no data or method. Ignore them.

Your own results say the same thing:

  • EA wiki: the sweep, FVG and kill-zone scalpers on gold are marginal or no-edge. The one promising SMC robot (SMC_Confluence) is in-sample only.
  • ../concepts/vwap_volume_profile_explained.md: on Nifty stocks the sweep + higher-time-frame checklist improved results in 26 of 36 comparisons. This is the best lead you have that a sweep filter adds something.
  • The wiki also found that most of your SMC robots enter at market and never wait for the retest, do not check that an FVG is still unfilled, and do not tie the order block to the break it caused. So the textbook version of SMC has not been tested by your code yet.

About ICT himself: Michael Huddleston has taught online for more than a decade and has no audited long-run track record. Critics also say his definitions change over time, which makes them hard to test. part Treat his videos as the source of the vocabulary, not as proof.

6. Turning the concepts into strategies you can test

Give each concept one written rule before testing. Suggested starting definitions (my proposals, not a standard; the thresholds are starting values to vary). Index 1 = the last closed bar, as in MT5; never read bar 0, which is still forming and repaints:

ConceptRule a computer can follow
Swing highA bar whose high is above the highs of N bars on each side (N = 3 to 5); confirmed only after the N bars close
BOSA close beyond the last confirmed swing in the trend direction
CHoCH / MSSThe first close beyond the last confirmed swing against the trend
Liquidity levelPrevious day high/low, session high/low (Asian range), or two swings within 0.1 × ATR of each other (equal highs/lows)
SweepA bar trades beyond a liquidity level and closes back inside it
DisplacementA bar with body ≥ 1.5 × the average body of the last 20 bars
FVG (bullish)low[1] > high[3] (three closed bars); the zone is valid until price trades through it
Order block (bullish)The last down-close bar before the displacement that caused a BOS; valid until price closes below it
Premium / discountAbove / below the 50% line of the current swing range
Kill zoneCommonly quoted ICT hours: London 02:00–05:00 and New York 07:00–10:00, New York time, with DST handled. Treat the hours as a setting to test

Then follow the Phase 4 rules already in the roadmap, with four additions:

  1. One concept at a time. Test "sweep" alone, then "sweep + displacement", then add the FVG retrace entry. Keep a piece only if it improves on the step before. A ten-condition checklist cannot tell you which part works.
  2. Random-entry benchmark with the same stop, target and session. Both outside tests above found SMC entries close to random, so this is the comparison that matters.
  3. Costs as a share of the stop. Measure spread + commission as a share of the stop distance. My rule of thumb (not sourced): above about 10% the idea rarely survives. The Northmark test measured 30–60% on 15-minute FX bars. This may be part of why your M1–M5 gold scalps are marginal; start on M15–H1.
  4. Enter on the retest, not at market, and check the zone is still unfilled. This is the gap between the textbook and your current EAs.

Suggested first experiments, cheapest first:

  • 0. Reverse or continue? At previous-day and Asian-session highs/lows, compare two entries with the same stop size: fade the sweep (close back inside) and follow the break (close beyond). Osler predicts the second; SMC trades the first. This one test tells you which side of the level has anything.
  • A. Sweep as a filter. Take your best non-SMC baseline (Supertrend + 200 EMA on gold). Does requiring a prior sweep of the previous day's or Asian-session high/low improve it out of sample?
  • B. The ICT 2022 model, written exactly: sweep of a session level → displacement that leaves an FVG and breaks structure → limit order at the FVG → stop beyond the sweep → target the opposite liquidity level. EURUSD and XAUUSD, M15, 3+ years of real ticks.
  • C. Fix and re-test what exists: SMC_Confluence out of sample (already step 2 of the wiki's next steps).
  • D. Later, Phase 7: the same setups on 6E or GC futures with real delta — does absorption or a delta flip at the sweep separate winners from losers?

No part of this promises profit. The roadmap's base rates still apply, and the honest prior from the open tests is that most SMC rules will not survive costs. The value of the work is finding out which piece, if any, does.
